rationale: The prompt requests channels containing messages the acting user (agent1) reacted to with 'eyes', correctly resolved as a multiple-selection route CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→REACTION. The one existing seeded reaction (agent1/eyes on message 1706110000.000100 in C03IJKL9012) is correctly captured as a match, and the second match (C_FRONTEND) is a planned addition, permissible at design stage. All three negatives isolate distinct real failure modes (wrong emoji by the same user in C_INFRA, correct emoji by a different user in C_MODEL, and authorship-vs-reaction substitution in C02EFGH5678), all grounded in real relations and channels the actor already belongs to per channel_members, so discovery via users.conversations/conversations.history/reactions.get is realistic. Binding note accurately reflects the three-way match condition (message_id, user_id, reaction_type) on the same reaction record. No hidden-ID or unsupported-capability issues, and answer_attributes (channel_name/channel_id) are legitimate table columns. The negatives are non-hinting and path-derived, giving strong quality without redundancy.
